name: MiraclePlus
tagline: China's YC-style accelerator, buying frontier technology at pre-seed prices
summary: MiraclePlus was founded in 2019 in Beijing by Lu Qi, the former Microsoft executive vice president and Baidu group president, as the independent successor to YC China after Y Combinator withdrew from the market. It runs the same shape of programme as its predecessor — two accelerator batches a year, a standard $300,000 cheque for 7% equity, three months of weekly partner office hours, and a Demo Day in front of more than a thousand investors — but applies it to Chinese hard-technology founders rather than consumer software. Ten batches in, the firm reports 612 funded startups, roughly 1,500 alumni founders and a combined portfolio valuation near RMB 90B, with a portfolio that skews heavily toward embodied intelligence, AI infrastructure and agent products.
shortSummary: MiraclePlus is a Beijing accelerator founded in 2019 by Lu Qi as the independent successor to YC China. It runs two batches a year with a standard US$300,000 cheque for 7% equity and a Demo Day. Its portfolio skews heavily toward embodied intelligence, AI infrastructure and agent products.
longSummary: MiraclePlus was founded in 2019 in Beijing by Lu Qi, the former Microsoft executive vice president and Baidu group president, as the independent successor to YC China after Y Combinator withdrew from the market. Ten batches in, the firm reports 612 funded startups, roughly 1,500 alumni founders and a combined portfolio valuation near RMB 90B.

thesis.heading: Frontier Technology at the Earliest Price
thesis.body: The firm states that over 99% of its investments sit in frontier innovation fields, and it deliberately funds projects other investors consider too early or too technical — buying deep-tech risk at a fixed pre-seed valuation rather than competing in priced rounds.

thesis.heading: Product-market Fit in Three Months
thesis.body: The programme's stated objective is to get a company ready to face investors within three months. Partners including Lu Qi run weekly one-on-one office hours — around 100 hours per project on average — focused on the single constraint blocking traction.

thesis.heading: Robotics and Embodied Intelligence
thesis.body: The most concentrated cluster in the portfolio: mobile robots, tactile sensing, actuators and simulation data. It reflects a view that China's manufacturing base gives embodied AI a cost and iteration advantage no software-only market can match.

thesis.heading: Compute and Agents as the Second Axis
thesis.body: Alongside hardware, the firm backs the inference and agent layer — SiliconFlow for model serving, HPC-AI Tech for distributed training, and consumer agent products such as Fellou and Macaron built by alumni founders.

portfolioGroups.heading: AI Portfolio
portfolioGroups.blurb: MiraclePlus-backed AI companies highlighted by the firm, spanning model infrastructure, embodied intelligence and agent products.

companies.name: SiliconFlow
companies.note: Model inference and serving platform giving developers low-cost access to open-source and Chinese foundation models.

companies.name: HPC-AI Tech
companies.note: Creator of Colossal-AI, an open-source system for distributed large-model training and inference.

companies.name: LightWheel AI
companies.note: Synthetic data and simulation platform supplying training data for robotics and autonomous driving models.

companies.name: Paxini
companies.note: Multi-dimensional tactile sensors and humanoid robots built around touch as the primary modality.

companies.name: Standard Robots
companies.note: Autonomous mobile robots for factory and warehouse logistics in electronics manufacturing.

companies.name: Fellou
companies.note: Agentic browser that plans and executes multi-step web tasks on the user's behalf.

companies.name: Macaron
companies.note: Consumer agent that generates small personal apps and workflows from natural-language requests.

companies.name: Zeroerr
companies.note: Direct-drive motors and actuator modules used in robot joints and precision motion systems.

companies.name: Jiliu Technology
companies.note: High-performance networking and interconnect for AI training clusters.

companies.name: Jiutian Ruixin
companies.note: Analogue in-memory computing chips for always-on, low-power edge perception.

companies.name: Gravity
companies.note: Domain-specific processors targeting data-centre workloads and AI acceleration.

companies.name: Jike Technology
companies.note: Consumer AI hardware and interaction devices built by an alumni founding team.
